**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

SOW Section 19 delivers the preferred position on the material terms:

- **Express warranty (p1059):** MSL warrants all Products, MSL-supplied materials/Parts and work conform in all material respects to IBM-furnished specifications, and are of specified quality, good workmanship and free from defect.
- **Duration (p1063, p1067, p1068):** stated periods in months for MSL Procured Parts and workmanship (figures redacted `[*]`), commencing on delivery to IBM, surviving acceptance testing and IBM's Product test procedure, and expressly covering latent defects — better than the preferred "12 months / 90 days" baseline in structure.
- **Remedy (p1077):** Failure Analysis, repair or replacement within a set turnaround at MSL's expense, with a **refund** of MSL's price and Parts prices if repair/replacement is not possible. Reinforced by epidemic-failure recall cost allocation (p1086) and a title warranty (p1075).
- **Disclaimer does not swallow the warranty (p1079/p1083):** Section 19.6 is an "in lieu of" exclusion of implied/other quality terms that expressly preserves "MSL'S WARRANTY OBLIGATIONS DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION 19." Far from the "AS IS" walk-away.

Noted in the rationale only, not flagged: no express "no malicious code" warranty, no standalone software conformance-to-documentation warranty (compliance with law sits separately at Section 16.4), and the durations are redacted. These are minor sub-elements rather than material failures of the fallback, so per the playbook's classification semantics they do not warrant a redline.
